text: For a moment he was no longer standing in the stairwell. He saw the ground as it had been centuries earlier—open and raw beneath a sky that looked exactly like the one above them now. The older city lay beneath the earth like a secret pressed between pages. Above it, thousands of men worked beneath the eyes of priests and kings. They were not building a new city. They were burying the old one.
speaker: Narrator

text: Massive stones were dragged across the ground by teams of exhausted workers. Ropes groaned. Men shouted. Overseers struck anyone who stopped moving. There was no celebration, no ceremony, no dedication—only the silence men used when they were afraid of being heard.
speaker: Narrator

text: One worker paused and looked down into the darkness of the unfinished structure. Then he dropped his tools and began screaming. The others turned. Several men dragged him away while he kicked and clawed at the ground. He screamed until the sound became raw and animal. A priest struck him across the mouth. The worker kept screaming.

text: His father stood in the same place. He was older than Zik remembered—hair streaked with gray, face thinner, clothing torn and stained with dust. He looked like a man who had been walking for years without ever reaching the place he intended to go. Then he looked straight toward Zik across the impossible distance. His expression was not fear. It was sorrow.
